concepts.why: The patient's presentation with a large polypoid mass obstructing the left nasal cavity, combined with the pathological findings of CD138-positive, CD56-positive, and EBV-positive cells, and gains of florescence signal at multiple loci, is consistent with Extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma, nasal type.
The gains of florescence signal at multiple loci, including 3q27 (BCL6), 8q24 (MYC), and 14q32 (IGH), are consistent with Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.

The patient's presentation with a large polypoid mass obstructing the left nasal cavity, combined with the pathological findings of CD138-positive and EBV-positive cells, is consistent with Plasmablastic lymphoma.

The patient's presentation with a large polypoid mass obstructing the left nasal cavity, combined with the pathological findings of CD138-positive, CD56-positive, and EBV-positive cells, is consistent with Nasal natural killer cell lymphoma.

The patient's presentation with a large polypoid mass obstructing the left nasal cavity, combined with the pathological findings of EBV-positive cells and gains of florescence signal at multiple loci, is consistent with Lymphomatoid granulomatosis.

The patient's presentation with a large polypoid mass obstructing the left nasal cavity, combined with the pathological findings of CD138-positive and CD56-positive cells, is consistent with Angiocentric lymphoma.
The CD20-negative and PAX5-negative findings are explained by plasma cell neoplasm, which is typically negative for these markers.

rationales.F06: CD20 negativity helps rule out Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma and Plasmablastic lymphoma.
